Run here: STZ-diabetic rat, Evans-blue blood-retinal-barrier leak (intravitreal VEGF Trap, VGT-NC-007).

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Korobelnik 2014 (PMID 25012934). Paired comparison: the trial paper does not cite the rat model. Redated to DA VINCI (NCT00789477; Do 2011, PMID 21546089, epub 2011-05-05; abstract read; registry results 2014-09-09), the first public DME-patient result on this track; VIVID/VISTA (Korobelnik 2014) confirmed it.

engagement.judgement: Judgement call on the readout: the rat model reads vascular permeability (Evans blue); its clinical counterpart is OCT central retinal thickness, a downstream readout of the same leak, so readout_tier is downstream and magnitude direction_only (dye extravasation normalised to non-diabetic levels versus um of retinal thickness are not commensurable). Model side is the FDA pharmacology review of BLA 125387 (studies VGT-NC-007 intravitreal and VGT-NC-008 systemic: Evans-blue concentrations 'equivalent to the levels seen in non-diabetic controls'), i.e. the product itself in the model. A direct free-VEGF readout exists for aflibercept only in nAMD (Fauser 2016, doi:10.1136/bjophthalmol-2015-308264, aqueous VEGF-A suppressed 67 +/- 14 days) and was not used because the model never measured VEGF. Registry: VIVID NCT01331681 results first posted 2014-09-09, VISTA NCT01363440 2015-04-20; epub 2014-07-08 is earlier, so year 2014.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled full text). The abstract names no study; the DME patient aqueous data are presumably the MP0112 phase I/II (Campochiaro 2013, PMID 23218689: aqueous MP0112 levels and 'neutralization of VEGF in aqueous humor for 8-12 weeks' after 0.4 mg). The reproduction claim rests on the abstract sentence 'The model quantitatively described abicipar-VEGF target engagement leading to rapid reduction of VEGF and a long duration of VEGF inhibition'. No numeric predicted-vs-observed comparison is given in the abstract, so magnitude is null. model_filed true: the EMA Rayoqta withdrawal assessment report (EMA/CHMP/279665/2020, section 3.2.2) describes 'an in silico mechanistic, multi-compartment PK model' built on ocular tissue data, with human abicipar and VEGF vitreal concentrations simulated over 52 weeks for the 2 mg phase 3 regimens, i.e. this model (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/withdrawal-report/withdrawal-assessment-report-rayoqta_en.pdf).

Direct readout tier: free VEGF and drug in aqueous humor. comparison_stated true because the paper itself sets the model against the patient data. The DME patients supply the context's patient side; nAMD data were pooled in the same refit. The EMA Rayoqta withdrawal assessment report (section 3.2.2, adopted 2020-05-28) states the same comparison in the regulator's words: 'the human model again fitted well against the measured abicipar concentrations in serum and aqueous humor from patients with nAMD and diabetic macular edema, respectively.'

dose.note: Rule 6 (earliest public date): DA VINCI phase 2 had a 2 mg q8w arm (3 monthly loads then every 8 weeks) that gained as much as monthly dosing at week 24 (2011). 2 mg every 8 weeks matched monthly dosing (10.7 vs 10.5-12.5 letters), inside the model's 10-12-week window; monkeys tolerated 4 mg/eye monthly.

dose.quote: Patients in the 4 VEGF Trap-Eye groups experienced mean visual acuity benefits ranging from +8.5 to +11.4 Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) letters versus only +2.5 letters in the laser group (P ≤ 0.0085 for each VEGF Trap-Eye group vs. laser).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Paired comparison: Korobelnik cites no PK model. Redated to DA VINCI (NCT00789477; Do 2011, PMID 21546089, epub 2011-05-05; abstract read; registry results 2014-09-09), the first public DME-patient result on this track; VIVID/VISTA (Korobelnik 2014) confirmed it.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the 2q8 regimen was chosen from a clinical observation, not from the model (FDA clinical pharmacology review of BLA 125387: the two-month interval 'was based on the observation from VGFT-OD-0508 that, at Week 8, improvements in visual acuity after a single 2-mg dose were similar to those obtained with 2 mg dosed monthly'). The model's 10-12-week prediction was nonetheless put to the test by the 2q8 arm and held, so same with magnitude within_2x (8-week interval held; the later direct measurement in nAMD, Fauser 2016, gave 67 +/- 14 days of aqueous VEGF suppression, just under the predicted 10-12 weeks). margin_stated true under decision 16: the same FDA package states monkeys took 0.5-4 mg/eye monthly for 9 doses with only mild, transient inflammation, and patients were dosed to 2 mg without the nasal toxicity seen at >= 2 mg/eye in monkeys (scored in safety). Abicipar's rabbit-to-human PK/PD model (Luu 2020, doi:10.1124/jpet.119.263178) was refitted to DME and nAMD patient aqueous-humour data, a refit rather than a tested prediction, and its DME phase 2 PALM (NCT02186119) has no posted results, so abicipar adds no DME dose entry.
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted duration of intravitreal VEGF-binding activity (10-12 weeks) versus the 8-week interval that held

dose.note: Abicipar blocked vascular permeability in the rabbit chronic retinal-neovascularisation model; no DME dosing comparison (PALM phase 2 unpublished). Run here: Rabbit chronic retinal-neovascularisation leak model (abicipar).
dose.quote: Abicipar was effective in cell-based and in vivo models of angiogenesis and vascular leak, blocking neovascularization in a mouse model of corneal neovascularization and vascular permeability in a rabbit model of chronic neovascularization.
dose.judgement: Second dose track, kept apart from the decay model because it is a different system with a different prediction (a leak-duration PD challenge rather than a PK extrapolation). Opened with abicipar, the first class member published in this model; abicipar's own DME trial (PALM, NCT02186119) posted no results, so the track stays untested until aflibercept 8 mg used the same model.

dose.note: Retrodiction ruling: the aflibercept 8 mg rabbit study was first public in the 2023 FDA review, after the same drug's own PHOTON/PULSAR topline (Regeneron press release, September 2022: 12- and 16-week regimens non-inferior), so it reproduces a known dose result: retro. Rabbit RNV model: 2 mg/eye (about 8 mg human) stayed leak-free longer than 0.5 mg; PHOTON 8q12/8q16 non-inferior to 2q8 at week 48. Run here: Rabbit chronic retinal-neovascularisation leak model (aflibercept 8 mg).
dose.quote: Aflibercept 8q12 and 8q16 demonstrated non-inferior BCVA gains to aflibercept 2q8 (BCVA mean change from baseline 8·8 letters [SD 9·0] in the 8q12 group, 7·9 letters [8·4] in the 8q16 group, and 9·2 letters [9·0] in the 2q8 group).
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Brown 2024 (PMID 38461843); the model side is read from the FDA pharmacology review of BLA 761355 (section 1.2). PHOTON topline press release: https://investor.regeneron.com/news-releases/news-release-details/aflibercept-8-mg-meets-primary-endpoints-two-global-pivotal (PR Newswire 301620404, September 2022; date from the release listing, page not opened).
dose.reason: Rabbit durability prediction held in PHOTON
dose.judgement: Year 2023 because the comparison was public with the FDA review and approval (August 2023) and the registry posting (2023-11-21) before the Lancet epub (2024-03-07). The FDA reviewer states the model's human prediction in so many words: the rabbit study 'support[s] the hypothesis that increasing the IVT dose of aflibercept in humans will result in a longer durability of effect', with 2 mg/eye in rabbit scaled to about 8 mg in humans by vitreous volume; the review does not set it beside PHOTON in one sentence, so comparison_stated false. The applicant's popPK (same package) predicted free-aflibercept ocular exposure of 15 weeks after 8 mg versus 8.7 weeks after 2 mg, which the reviewer flagged as unconfirmed by ocular sampling; PHOTON's 12- and 16-week intervals held, hence within_2x. margin_stated true: the same review gives an ocular NOAEL of 7 mg/eye (1.8-fold the 8 mg dose on vitreous volume) and PHOTON reached the dose without that toxicity; nasal turbinate findings had no NOAEL at 4-7 mg/eye and were accepted on a systemic exposure margin (about 3-fold), scored in safety.
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted ocular free-drug duration (15 vs 8.7 weeks) versus the 12-16-week intervals that held

The model is the applicant's, built on pooled plasma PK that includes CANDELA, PULSAR and PHOTON; it is a different system from the academic rabbit-half-life decay model (Stewart 2008) and from the rabbit chronic-RNV leak model, so it gets its own model_id.

dose.note: PopPK predicted free aflibercept above ocular LLOQ for 15 weeks after 8 mg vs 8.7 weeks after 2 mg; PHOTON 8q12/8q16 non-inferior to 2q8. Built on PHOTON data, so a retrodiction.
dose.short: Post-hoc popPK: 15 vs 8.7 weeks, PHOTON held
dose.srcLabel: FDA Eylea HD clinical pharmacology review 2023
dose.quote: The median time for free aflibercept to reach the adjusted LLOQ in the ocular compartment increased from 8.7 weeks after a 2 mg IVT dose to 15 weeks after an 8 mg IVT dose
dose.confidence_note: The reviewer flagged the ocular prediction as unconfirmed: 'as there is no observed ocular concentration of aflibercept to confirm the prediction, such interpretation should be treated with caution.' Regeneron's 2026 integrated popPK (PMID 42381356, 16 trials, 2744 participants) restates the same system's prediction (14 weeks vs 9-9.5 weeks); same system, no new status.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction under decision 10, not a prospective dose prediction: the popPK dataset carries PHOTON's own plasma PK (study VGFTe-HD-DME-1934, primary completion 2022-05-30) and the BLA was filed after the 48-week readout, so the 15-week ocular estimate was produced with the q12/q16 answer known. It reproduced the result (12-16-week intervals non-inferior to 2q8 in PHOTON: Brown 2024, registry 2023-11-21), hence retro, within_2x. comparison_stated true: the review itself ties the model's longer ocular exposure to the HD drug effect ('Exploratory analyses suggest the slower ocular clearance and longer duration of free aflibercept ocular exposure of HD aflibercept contribute to the drug effect of HD aflibercept'). Dated 2024 because the only public carrier of the prediction is the review, posted in the nda/2024 folder; the 2023 label does not state the ocular LLOQ times. If the atlas treats FDA reviews as public at approval (2023-08-18), the year is 2023. No tolerability margin is stated by this model (margin_stated false); the ocular NOAEL sits on the toxicology track.
dose.magnitude_basis: predicted free-aflibercept ocular exposure 15 weeks (8 mg) vs 8.7 weeks (2 mg) against the 12- and 16-week PHOTON intervals that held

PALM (NCT02186119; abicipar 2 mg at weeks 0, 4, 8 then q12 or q8 vs ranibizumab; completed 2015-06) is the only DME trial of the regimen: no registry results, no peer-reviewed report found in Europe PMC. The q12 result in nAMD (CEDAR/SEQUOIA, Kunimoto 2020, doi 10.1016/j.ophtha.2020.03.035) is outside this context. model_filed true: the EMA Rayoqta withdrawal assessment report (EMA/CHMP/279665/2020, section 3.2.2) describes 'an in silico mechanistic, multi-compartment PK model' built on ocular tissue data, with human abicipar and VEGF vitreal concentrations simulated over 52 weeks for the 2 mg phase 3 regimens, i.e. this model (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/withdrawal-report/withdrawal-assessment-report-rayoqta_en.pdf).

dose.judgement: The abicipar 2 mg q8/q12 regimens had already been dosed in DME (PALM, 2014-2015) and nAMD (CEDAR/SEQUOIA, 2015-2018) before the model was published, so any scoring would be a retrodiction under decision 10; but no DME patient result is admissible (no registry results, no paper, no regulator document for DME), so the cell stays untested with the model named. The EMA report adds that the model's 52-week simulations of 2Q8/2Q12 'resulted in permanent vitreal abicipar concentrations above the calculated IC50 value for VEGF inhibition' and 'support dose selection and treatment regimen of 2 mg/eye 2Q8/2Q12'; the regimen was nonetheless already in PALM and CEDAR/SEQUOIA before the model was public.

efficacy.note: STZ-diabetic rat Evans-blue leak, 1-week diabetes: VEGF TrapA40 (aflibercept precursor) normalised permeability; later filed as VGT-NC-007/008 with intravitreal VEGF Trap. Run here: STZ-diabetic rat, Evans-blue blood-retinal-barrier leak (VEGF TrapA40, systemic).
efficacy.short: VEGF Trap abolished diabetic retinal leak
efficacy.quote: Diabetes-induced blood-retinal barrier breakdown was dose-dependently inhibited with VEGF TrapA(40), with 25 mg/kg producing complete inhibition of the diabetes-induced increases (P < 0.05).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no DOI (IOVS 2001). The model is early leak in rats with no macula and no oedema, a permeability surrogate rather than DME itself.
efficacy.judgement: model_filed true for the track as a whole: the FDA pharmacology review of BLA 125387 (2011) lists VGT-NC-007 (intravitreal VEGF Trap, 3 ug, in diabetic Sprague-Dawley rats) and VGT-NC-008, and the summary review states 'reduced leakage from retinal vessels in the diabetic rat model'. efficacy.note: Rule 6 (earliest public date): DA VINCI phase 2 primary endpoint (BCVA at week 24) met, +8.5 to +11.4 vs +2.5 letters on laser (2011). Primary endpoint met: BCVA +10.5 to +12.5 letters on aflibercept vs +0.2/+1.2 on laser at week 52 in both phase 3 trials. Run here: STZ-diabetic rat, Evans-blue blood-retinal-barrier leak (intravitreal VEGF Trap, VGT-NC-007).
efficacy.short: DA VINCI then VIVID/VISTA beat laser
efficacy.quote: Patients in the 4 VEGF Trap-Eye groups experienced mean visual acuity benefits ranging from +8.5 to +11.4 Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) letters versus only +2.5 letters in the laser group (P ≤ 0.0085 for each VEGF Trap-Eye group vs. laser).

efficacy.judgement: The rat model predicts reduced vascular leak, not vision; the primary endpoint is BCVA, so magnitude is direction_only on a permeability-to-letters basis. Model side is the FDA pharmacology review of BLA 125387 (VGT-NC-007/008, the product in the model). The monkey laser-CNV model (Nork 2011, doi:10.1001/archophthalmol.2011.210) is the nAMD model and is not opened here as a DME track. No class member failed in DME, so not neg. Registry: VIVID NCT01331681 results 2014-09-09, VISTA NCT01363440 2015-04-20.

patient_trials.quote: Patients in the 4 VEGF Trap-Eye groups experienced mean visual acuity benefits ranging from +8.5 to +11.4 Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) letters versus only +2.5 letters in the laser group (P ≤ 0.0085 for each VEGF Trap-Eye group vs. laser).

Mean BCVA gains from baseline to week 52 in the IAI 2q4 and 2q8 groups versus the laser group were 12.5 and 10.7 versus 0.2 letters (P < 0.0001) in VISTA, and 10.5 and 10.7 versus 1.2 letters (P < 0.0001) in VIVID.
The corresponding proportions of eyes gaining ≥ 15 letters were 41.6% and 31.1% versus 7.8% (P < 0.0001) in VISTA, and 32.4% and 33.3% versus 9.1% (P < 0.0001) in VIVID.

Aflibercept 8q12 and 8q16 demonstrated non-inferior BCVA gains to aflibercept 2q8 (BCVA mean change from baseline 8·8 letters [SD 9·0] in the 8q12 group, 7·9 letters [8·4] in the 8q16 group, and 9·2 letters [9·0] in the 2q8 group).

One track for the class's repeat-dose intravitreal toxicology in large animals: abicipar's package (rabbit, dog, monkey) is the same kind of system with the same prediction (injection-related intraocular inflammation), so it joins this track rather than opening another under this run's track-identity rule.

safety.short: No nasal erosions in monitored patients
safety.quote: Patients were monitored for this adverse effect in clinical trials and no similar pathology was seen.
safety.confidence_note: OCRed bundle text (sources/125387/125387Orig1s000SumR.txt, section 4 and 8.1: 'Erosions found in animal studies were not reported in patients.'). Patient side is nAMD (VIEW 1/2), imported.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: same rather than contra. The monkey showed nasal turbinate erosions at 2 and 4 mg/eye, the clinical dose, but the stated prediction the regulator acted on was exposure-scaled: at the 0.5 mg/eye NOAEL systemic exposure was 42-56 times the human exposure at 2 mg, and the label (13.2) carries that margin; a dedicated ENT sub-study (about 160 patients) found none, so the margin held. The mild, transient anterior-segment/vitreous inflammation the monkeys showed at every dose also appeared in patients at low rates. A re-scorer who reads v3's 'a predicted harm that never appeared in patients is a wrong prediction' literally, ignoring the stated margin, should flip this to contra with magnitude opposite. source_calls_it is 'over_predicted' because the summary review itself calls the finding unexpected and records that no similar pathology was seen. imported_from is age-related macular degeneration (VIEW); DME patients were examined for the same finding only in 2023 (entry below).
safety.magnitude_basis: nasal turbinate erosion predicted only above a stated 42-56x systemic exposure margin and not seen; mild intraocular inflammation predicted and seen

safety.note: Retrodiction and imported-harm rulings: DME patients were measured first (Campochiaro 2013, MP0112 phase I/II, epub 2012-12-04: ocular inflammation in 11 of 18, 61%), so they set the status, and abicipar's animal toxicology was first public only in the 2020 EMA report, after that same-drug result: it reproduced it, retro. EMA: intravitreal abicipar inflamed most animals tested; CEDAR/SEQUOIA intraocular inflammation 15.4%/15.3% vs 0.3% on ranibizumab led to the 2020 FDA CRL. Run here: Rabbit, dog and cynomolgus repeat-dose intravitreal toxicology (abicipar).
safety.quote: Intravitreal injection of abicipar resulted in intraocular inflammation in most of the animals tested.
safety.confidence_note: EMA/415176/2020, section 3.2.6 (page 36 of 132), read from pdftotext; the next sentences read 'Intraocular inflammation also occurs in human. Correlation with development of anti-drug antibodies could not be unambiguously clarified by nonclinical data.' Patient figures (IOI 15.4% Q8, 15.3% Q12, 0.3% ranibizumab) are from Kunimoto 2020, doi:10.1016/j.ophtha.2020.03.035, whose abstract was read in part. DME patient side: Campochiaro 2013, doi 10.1016/j.ajo.2012.09.032, abstract: 'Ocular inflammation was observed in 11 patients (61%) and was severe in 1.' No earlier public source of the abicipar animal toxicology was found.
safety.judgement: Judgement call against the brief's framing of abicipar as an intraocular-inflammation miss: the regulator's own nonclinical summary says the animals showed the harm ('most of the animals tested'), that it tracked process impurities (drug substance from the later process gave 'lower incidences and/or less pronounced manifestations of intraocular inflammation in rabbits'), and that it also occurs in humans, so the model's prediction held in direction and is scored same, strengthening the track; the clinical failure (FDA complete response letter 26 June 2020 citing the IOI rate, AbbVie press release; EU and Japan filings withdrawn) was a decision to proceed despite the signal, not a model error. magnitude direction_only on incidence (most animals versus 15% of patients). The model side and the comparison are both in the EMA document (comparison_stated true). imported_from age-related macular degeneration: CEDAR NCT02462928 results 2020-07-28, SEQUOIA NCT02462486 2020-07-30, MAPLE NCT03539549 2020-08-03 (IOI 8.9% after the host-cell-protein reduction, Callanan 2023, doi:10.2147/OPTH.S405994); abicipar's DME phase 2 PALM (NCT02186119) posted no results. The exact CHMP date of the withdrawal report was not verified; year 2020 from its reference number and the July 2020 withdrawal.
safety.magnitude_basis: incidence of intraocular inflammation: most animals versus 15.4%/15.3% of patients
safety.population: Centre-involved DME (MP0112/abicipar phase I/II) plus nAMD phase 3

safety.model: Repeat-dose intravitreal toxicology in rabbit, dog and cynomolgus monkey
safety.note: Safety ruling: monkeys again showed nasal turbinate erosion at 4-7 mg/eye with no NOAEL; DME patients in PHOTON (and PULSAR) showed no nasomucosal signal, so the predicted harm did not appear (contra, opposite), now in this disease's own patients. 8 mg program: monkeys again mild inflammation, nasal erosions at 4-7 mg/eye; PHOTON (DME) and PULSAR showed no nasomucosal signal. Run here: Cynomolgus repeat-dose intravitreal toxicology (aflibercept 8 mg, 3 and 6 months).
safety.short: PHOTON: no nasomucosal signal at 8 mg
safety.quote: an analysis of treatment emergent adverse events of nasomucosal findings was conducted with no indication of a safety signal in the 8 mg aflibercept groups compared to 2 mg.
safety.confidence_note: Bundle text sources/761355/761355Orig1s000PharmR.txt, section 1.2; the sentence is attributed 'Per the Applicant' and names PULSAR, CANDELA and PHOTON (DME phase 2/3). First DME-patient comparison on this track; subjects are DME plus nAMD patients.
safety.reason: Nasal erosion predicted, absent in PHOTON
safety.judgement: Strengthening entry: the first comparison made in DME patients themselves (PHOTON, NCT04429503, results posted 2023-11-21). The 8 mg monkey studies repeated the 2011 picture (ocular findings 'limited to generally mild, transient ocular inflammation', ocular NOAEL 7 mg/eye; nasal turbinate erosion at 4 and 7 mg/eye with no NOAEL, accepted on a roughly 3-fold systemic exposure margin at the 0.5 mg/eye NOAEL) and patients at 8 mg showed no nasomucosal signal, so the stated margin held again; comparison_stated true because the review places the monkey finding and the clinical analysis together. PHOTON ocular adverse events were similar across arms (Brown 2024). Status does not change.
safety.magnitude_basis: nasal turbinate erosion predicted above a stated exposure margin and not seen; mild intraocular inflammation predicted and seen
